title: WPSB/221/2012 of S.D. MEHTA, EXECUTIVE ENGINEER and ORS. Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND and ORS.

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/B) No. 221 of 2012
S.D. Mehta and others ............Petitioners
Versus
State of Uttarakhand & others .............Respondents
Mr. Alok Dalakoti, Advocate holding brief of Mr. A.K. Joshi, Advocate for the
petitioners.
Mr. K.P. Upadhyaya, Chief Standing Counsel for State of Uttarakhand / respondent nos.
1 to 3.
Mr. P.S. Rawat, Advocate for respondent nos. 4 and 5.
Coram:Hon'ble Barin Ghosh, C.J.
 Hon'ble U.C. Dhyani, J.
Barin Ghosh, C.J. (Oral)
 The provision, contained in Section 3(7) of the Uttar
Pradesh Public Services (Reservation for Scheduled Castes,
Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes) Act, 1994, has
already been struck down by this Court. A similar prayer to that
effect has been made in the present writ petition. While,
however, making the prayer for striking down the provision of
the said Act, petitioners have not even bothered to look at the
provision of the Act and, accordingly, have not mentioned
correctly the name of the Act. In addition to that, petitioners
wanted Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe category of
employees to be outside creamy layer. The fact that the concept
of creamy layer does not apply to Scheduled Caste and Scheduled
Tribe category of employees was not taken note of at the time of
filing the writ petition. We gave several opportunities to the
learned counsel for the petitioners to show us that the concept of
creamy layer applies to Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe
category of employees. The learned counsel from time to time
made submissions on several dates, but failed to establish the
same. Today, a misconceived amendment application has been

2
filed, where an additional prayer has been incorporated in relation
to promotion in reservation along with Roster dated 31st August
2001 and maintaining of separate eligibility list for Scheduled
Castes and Scheduled Tribes. In view of striking down of
Section 3(7) of the said Act, these prayers have become otiose.
These misconceived writ petitions are being filed and the Court's
time is being unnecessarily wasted by the petitioners.
2. We, accordingly, dismiss the writ petition along with
the amendment application (CLMA No. 7375 of 2012) with costs
assessed at `500/- to be paid by the petitioners, within seven
days from today with State Legal Services Authority,
Uttarakhand.
(U.C. Dhyani, J.) (Barin Ghosh, C.J.)
 20.07.2012 20.07.2012
Rathour
